Reproducing Peterson et al. (2021) from dandiset 000055¶

Paper. Peterson SM, Singh SH, Wang NXR, Rao RPN, Brunton BW (2021). Behavioral and neural variability of naturalistic arm movements. eNeuro 8(3), ENEURO.0007-21.2021. doi:10.1523/ENEURO.0007-21.2021. The claims file was written from the version of record in Europe PMC (PMC8225404): main text, Methods, legends, Tables 1 and 2 and the legends of the Extended Data figures.

Dataset. DANDI:000055 (AJILE12), version 0.220127.0436. The paper cites no DANDI version: its data statement points to the curated epochs on Figshare, and the dandiset was published later. This is the only published version, and the draft lists the same 55 files with the same total size, so the published version is pinned. The files are streamed; nothing is downloaded.

What the dataset holds. 12 subjects and 55 subject-days of preprocessed ECoG (500 Hz), pose of nine key points (30 frames per second), 8088 contralateral wrist movement events with the paper's ten features, coarse behaviour labels, and an electrode table with MNI positions, a good flag and the paper's regression R2 per electrode. Sex and age are not in it.

Outside input. The projection of electrodes onto the eight AAL regions is the paper's own output on Figshare (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.12114408.v1), used for the region claims (data: with_inputs) and checked by the link claim roi-projection-link.

Event sets. Reading a is every event in the files. Reading b drops ECoG segments with missing samples, with power below 0 dB or with 115-125 Hz power more than 3 SD above the subject's segments (Methods); the summary of segment power these tests use is an assumption (helper docstring). The false positives the paper removed are not marked in the files, so they cannot be dropped.

The notebook reads about 8000 ECoG segments of 10 s from 55 files of 8 to 20 GB each; that step took 20 to 35 minutes in recent runs (the time is printed below). The regression models take a few minutes.

      f"{time.time() - started:.0f} s")

In [3]:
# One table of events. Time of day from the midnight clock of the files (see the helper).
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    e = s["events"].copy()
    e["subject"], e["day"], e["k"] = s["subject"], s["day"], np.arange(len(e))
    rows.append(e)
ev = pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True)
ev = ev.rename(columns={"Reach_magnitude_px": "magnitude", "Reach_angle_degrees": "angle_file",
                        "Onset_speed_px_per_sec": "speed", "Speech_ratio": "speech",
                        "Bimanual_ratio": "bimanual_ratio", "Bimanual_overlap": "bimanual_overlap",
                        "Bimanual_class": "bimanual_class"})
# The files' angle is atan2(dy, dx) in image coordinates (checked below); the paper's angle
# negates it (y up) and folds 90-270 degrees onto 90 to -90 (Methods; code).
ev["angle"] = ajile.fold_angle(-ev["angle_file"])
ev["hour"] = ev["start_time"] / 3600.0
ev["tod_bin"] = np.clip((ev["hour"] // 8).astype(int), 0, 2)
FEATURES = ["day", "hour", "duration", "magnitude", "angle", "speed", "speech",
            "bimanual_ratio", "bimanual_overlap", "bimanual_class"]
print(len(ev), "events")

8088 events

info = pd.DataFrame([{
    "subject": s["subject"], "day": s["day"], "subject_id": s["subject_id"], "session_id": s["session_id"],
    "session_start_time": s["session_start_time"], "electrodes": len(s["electrodes"]),
    "good": int(s["electrodes"]["good"].sum()), "events": len(s["events"]), "wrist": s["reach_event_desc"],
    "ecog_hours": round(s["ecog_shape"][0] / s["ecog_rate"] / 3600, 2), "ecog_Hz": s["ecog_rate"],

The files hold 12 subjects and 55 subject-days, ECoG at 500 Hz and pose at 30 frames per second. The ECoG is stored with a conversion of 1e-6 to volts, so the stored values are microvolts; the pose is labelled meters but holds pixels (the data descriptor gives pixels, and the values span hundreds). The subject has no sex or age in the files or the archive's metadata. Three files hold less than 24 h of ECoG and start later (S01 day 7, S04 day 3, S06 day 3); the clocks of these files are checked below.

The reaches table has the same nine columns in every file, and none marks false positives or verified events. The electrode groups whose description says depth are listed above beside the data descriptor's Table 2; S10 and S11 are counted differently there (see claim cohort).

# Reach angle convention: angle and magnitude from the wrist trace (onset to the largest
# displacement within the reach), compared with the files' values.
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    w = "R_Wrist" if s["reach_event_desc"] == "r_wrist" else "L_Wrist"
    tr = s["wrist"][w]
    for k, d in enumerate(s["events"].duration.values):
        n = int(round(d * ajile.POSE_HZ))
        seg = tr[k, 45:46 + min(n, 45)]
        if np.isnan(seg).any():
            continue
        dd = seg - seg[0]
        r = np.linalg.norm(dd, axis=1)
        j = r.argmax()
        rows.append((s["events"]["Reach_angle_degrees"].values[k], np.degrees(np.arctan2(dd[j, 1], dd[j, 0])),
                     s["events"]["Reach_magnitude_px"].values[k], r[j], d <= 1.5))
ang = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["file_angle", "trace_angle", "file_mag", "trace_mag", "within_window"])
circ = lambda a, b: np.abs((a - b + 180) % 360 - 180)
a = ang[ang.within_window]
print(f"{len(a)} reaches of at most 1.5 s with a full trace")
print("median |file angle - trace angle|, image coordinates:", round(np.median(circ(a.file_angle, a.trace_angle)), 2),
      "deg; with the trace angle negated (y up):", round(np.median(circ(a.file_angle, -a.trace_angle)), 2), "deg")
print("median file magnitude / trace magnitude:", round(np.median(a.file_mag / a.trace_mag), 3))
print("Folded angle (paper convention, +90 up): share of events above 0:", round((ev.angle > 0).mean(), 3))

Folded angle (paper convention, +90 up): share of events above 0: 0.683

The files' reach angle is the angle of the reach in image coordinates (y pointing down), not yet negated, so upward reaches have negative values; the paper's angle (+90 for upward) is its negation folded onto -90 to 90, as the code does. The files do not say which convention they use. The magnitudes match the traces.

In [9]:
# Clock of the pose and of the event times: contralateral wrist displacement from its mean
# position over -1.5 to -1 s, at the events and at the events shifted by -30 s.
def median_disp(tr, base_slice=slice(0, 16)):
    base = np.nanmean(tr[:, base_slice], 1)
    return np.nanmedian(np.linalg.norm(tr - base[:, None], axis=2), 0)

rows = []
for s in sessions:
    w = "R_Wrist" if s["reach_event_desc"] == "r_wrist" else "L_Wrist"
    m = median_disp(s["wrist"][w])
    rows.append({"subject": s["subject"], "day": s["day"], "disp_at_-1s": m[15].round(1),
                 "disp_at_0s": m[45].round(1), "disp_at_+1s": m[75].round(1)})
clk = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(clk.to_string(index=False))
print("Sessions where the contralateral wrist moves less than 10 pixels by +1 s:",
      clk[clk["disp_at_+1s"] < 10][["subject", "day"]].values.tolist())

In every file the contralateral wrist is still before the event time and moves after it, so the pose and the event table share a clock, including in the three files with less than 24 h of ECoG (whose events lie between 8 and 24 h). The shifted control needs the ECoG and is below.

Sleep labels fall mostly in the first hours of the file clock, which fits files that start at midnight local time. The files' session_start_time of 19:00 at UTC-5 is midnight UTC, so the stated time zone is not the local one; the three late files have start times of 03:07 to 03:31 at UTC-5, the start of their ECoG (checked below). The hour of an event is taken from the file clock.

ECoG: projection matrices and event segments¶

The paper's projection of electrodes onto the eight regions (AAL atlas through the Measure Projection Toolbox) is taken from its own output on Figshare (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.12114408.v1), which the claims file names as the paper's output of that step. Claim roi-projection-link checks that its rows can be matched to the dataset's electrodes. The bad electrodes are those of each subject's first file, as the paper's code takes them.

# Per-event ECoG measures, aligned with the event table.
REG = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(ajile.ROI_NAMES)}
ev["ok"] = np.concatenate([r["ok"] for r in ecog])
for key in ["q_all", "q_hf", "q_log"]:
    ev[key] = np.concatenate([r[key] for r in ecog])
spec = np.full((len(ev), 8, len(ajile.FREQS), len(ajile.TIMES)), np.nan, dtype=np.float32)
i = 0
for r in ecog:
    for ok, sp in zip(r["ok"], r["roi_spec"]):
        if ok:
            spec[i] = sp
        i += 1
for kind in ["roi_band", "roi_band_raw"]:
    for meas in ["lfb_mean", "lfb_median", "hfb_mean", "hfb_median"]:
        vals = np.full((len(ev), 8), np.nan)
        i = 0
        for r in ecog:
            for ok, b in zip(r["ok"], r[kind]):
                if ok:
                    vals[i] = b[meas]
                i += 1
        for reg, j in REG.items():
            ev[f"{kind}:{reg}:{meas}"] = vals[:, j]
# Bad segments (Methods): power below 0 dB, or 115-125 Hz power more than 3 SD above the mean
# of the subject's segments. False positives are not marked in the files (see the data check).
thr = ev[ev.ok].groupby("subject").q_hf.agg(lambda v: v.mean() + 3 * v.std())
ev["bad_missing"] = ev.ok & ~np.isfinite(ev.q_all)          # segments with missing (NaN) samples
ev["bad_low"] = ev.q_all < 0
ev["bad_hf"] = ev.q_hf > ev.subject.map(thr)
ev["keep_b"] = ev.ok & ~ev.bad_missing & ~ev.bad_low & ~ev.bad_hf
TIMES, FREQS = ajile.TIMES, ajile.FREQS
print("Events with a full ECoG segment:", int(ev.ok.sum()), "of", len(ev))
print("Segments with missing (NaN) samples:", int(ev.bad_missing.sum()), "in",
      ev[ev.bad_missing].groupby(["subject", "day"]).size().to_dict())
print("Segments below 0 dB:", int(ev.bad_low.sum()), "; 115-125 Hz above 3 SD:", int((ev.bad_hf & ~ev.bad_low).sum()),
      "; kept (reading b):", int(ev.keep_b.sum()))
print("Other reading of the 0 dB test (mean of the log density below 0 dB):", int((ev.q_log < 0).sum()), "of",
      int(ev.ok.sum()), "segments would go, so that reading is not usable")
print(ev[ev.ok].groupby("subject")[["q_all", "q_hf"]].agg(["min", "median", "max"]).round(1).to_string())

In [16]:
# Clock of the ECoG against the events: precentral and postcentral band power change from the
# -1.5 to -1 s baseline to 0-0.5 s, at the event time and at a pseudo-event 3 s earlier
# (-3 to -2.5 s against -4.5 to -4 s) in the same segments; median over events per file.
ti = lambda lo, hi: np.nonzero((TIMES >= lo - 1e-6) & (TIMES <= hi + 1e-6))[0]
lf = np.nonzero((FREQS >= 8) & (FREQS <= 32))[0]
hf = np.nonzero((FREQS >= 76) & (FREQS <= 100))[0]
def band_change(sp, band, t_on, t_base):
    return sp[..., band, :][..., t_on].mean((-1, -2)) - sp[..., band, :][..., t_base].mean((-1, -2))
rows = []
for (sub, day), g in ev[ev.keep_b].groupby(["subject", "day"]):
    sp = spec[g.index][:, [REG["precentral"], REG["postcentral"]]]
    row = {"subject": sub, "day": day, "n": len(g)}
    for name, band in [("HFB", hf), ("LFB", lf)]:
        true = band_change(sp, band, ti(0, 0.5), ti(-1.5, -1))
        pseudo = band_change(sp, band, ti(-3, -2.5), ti(-4.5, -4))
        best = np.argmax(np.abs(np.median(true, 0)))
        row[f"{name}_event"] = round(float(np.median(true[:, best])), 2)
        row[f"{name}_pseudo"] = round(float(np.median(pseudo[:, best])), 2)
    rows.append(row)
clock = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(clock.to_string(index=False))
clock_ok = (clock.HFB_event > 0) & (clock.LFB_event < 0) & (clock.HFB_event > clock.HFB_pseudo) & (clock.LFB_event < clock.LFB_pseudo)
print("Files with HFB up, LFB down at the event and both larger than at the pseudo-event:", int(clock_ok.sum()), "of", len(clock))
print("Files where this does not hold:", clock[~clock_ok][["subject", "day"]].values.tolist())

# of the helper (ECoG ends at midnight) against no offset (ECoG starts at midnight).
late = [s for s in sessions if ajile.ecog_offset(s) > 1]
alt = ajile.load_ecog(ajile.ecog_jobs(late, weights, offset=False), workers=3)
for s, r in zip(late, alt):
    g = ev[(ev.subject == s["subject"]) & (ev.day == s["day"]) & ev.keep_b]
    pre = REG["precentral"]
    a_h = band_change(spec[g.index][:, pre], hf, ti(0, 0.5), ti(-1.5, -1))
    a_l = band_change(spec[g.index][:, pre], lf, ti(0, 0.5), ti(-1.5, -1))
    sp_b = np.array([x[pre] for x, ok in zip(r["roi_spec"], r["ok"]) if ok and np.isfinite(x[pre]).all()])
    b_h = band_change(sp_b, hf, ti(0, 0.5), ti(-1.5, -1)) if len(sp_b) else np.array([np.nan])
    b_l = band_change(sp_b, lf, ti(0, 0.5), ti(-1.5, -1)) if len(sp_b) else np.array([np.nan])
    print(f"S{s['subject']} day {s['day']}: offset {ajile.ecog_offset(s):.1f} s; with offset {len(a_h)} events, "
          f"precentral HFB {np.median(a_h):+.2f} dB, LFB {np.median(a_l):+.2f} dB; without offset {len(sp_b)} events in "
          f"range, HFB {np.median(b_h):+.2f} dB, LFB {np.median(b_l):+.2f} dB; ReachEvents minus offset-corrected "
          f"times, max |diff| {np.max(np.abs(s['reach_event_times'] - (s['events'].start_time.values - ajile.ecog_offset(s)))):.3f} s")

Claim roi-projection-link¶

The rows of the paper's projection matrices (Figshare) can be matched one to one to the dataset's electrodes, and the weights fit the electrodes' positions.

In [19]:
cent_rows = {}
rows = []
rng_link = np.random.default_rng(55)
for sub in SUBJECTS:
    df = roi_mats[sub]
    el = [s for s in sessions if s["subject"] == sub][0]["electrodes"]
    n_rows = len(df) - 1
    zero = np.nonzero(df.iloc[1:].transpose().mean().values == 0)[0]
    cen = pd.read_csv(roi_meta[f"aal_{sub}_ROIcentroids_Lside.csv"][0])
    cen = cen.iloc[[df.columns.get_loc(c) for c in ajile.ROI_COLUMNS]].to_numpy(float)
    w = weights[sub]
    xyz = el[["x", "y", "z"]].to_numpy(float).copy()
    xyz[:, 0] = -np.abs(xyz[:, 0])                       # right hemisphere mirrored to the left
    dist = np.linalg.norm(xyz[:, None, :] - cen[None], axis=2)
    use = w.sum(1) > 0
    agree = np.mean(np.argmax(w[use], 1) == np.argmin(dist[use], 1))
    null = np.mean([np.mean(np.argmax(w[use], 1) == np.argmin(dist[use][rng_link.permutation(use.sum())], 1))
                    for _ in range(200)])
    rho = stats.spearmanr(w[use].ravel(), -dist[use].ravel())[0]
    rows.append({"subject": sub, "electrodes": len(el), "matrix_rows": n_rows, "all_zero_rows": len(zero),
                 "zero_row_groups": ",".join(sorted(set(el.group_name.values[zero]))) if n_rows == len(el) else
                 f"rows {zero.min()}-{zero.max()} (beyond the {len(el)} electrodes)",
                 "rows_used": len(w), "top_weight_is_nearest_centroid": round(agree, 3),
                 "same_with_order_shuffled": round(null, 3), "spearman_weight_vs_proximity": round(rho, 3)})

Result: not reproduced. The dataset holds 211 to 996 events per subject (median 770.5); after dropping segments with missing samples, below 0 dB or with high 115-125 Hz power, 211 to 979 (median 739). The fewest (211 against 151 +- 15.1) and the median (against 640 +- 64) are outside tolerance under both readings; the most is within. The files hold 8088 events, where the data descriptor states 6931, and no event is marked as a false positive. The reaches table has the same nine columns in all 55 files and none marks an event as a false positive or as verified, so reading b cannot drop the false positives: the outcome rests on reading a and on reading b without that step.

Claim fig2-reach-shape¶

Reach duration and reach magnitude vary little across subjects, with most reaches lasting under 2 s and covering under 200 pixels, and reach angle distributions tend to be bimodal with peaks near +90 and -90 degrees, with few side-to-side reaches.

In [23]:
from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde
grid = np.linspace(-90, 90, 361)
def bimodal(a):
    dens = gaussian_kde(a, bw_method="scott")(grid)
    peaks = [i for i in range(1, len(grid) - 1) if dens[i] > dens[i - 1] and dens[i] >= dens[i + 1]]
    # ends of the range count as maxima when the density rises towards them
    if dens[0] > dens[1]:
        peaks.append(0)
    if dens[-1] > dens[-2]:
        peaks.append(len(grid) - 1)
    top = sorted(peaks, key=lambda i: -dens[i])[:2]
    locs = sorted(grid[top])
    zero = dens[np.argmin(np.abs(grid))]
    ok = len(locs) == 2 and abs(locs[0] + 90) <= 15 and abs(locs[1] - 90) <= 15 and zero < dens[top].min()
    return ok, locs, zero / dens[top].min() if len(top) else np.nan

In [25]:
# Sensitivity, not the criterion: how far a Gaussian KDE without boundary correction pulls peaks
# in from the ends of a bounded range. Synthetic folded angles whose density peaks exactly at
# +-90 (90 minus a half-normal of SD 25 degrees, either sign), and the same KDE with the data
# reflected at -90 and +90 (a standard boundary correction).
rng_kde = np.random.default_rng(2)
def kde_peaks(a, reflect=False):
    data = np.r_[a, -180 - a, 180 - a] if reflect else a
    kde = gaussian_kde(data, bw_method="scott")
    if reflect:
        kde.set_bandwidth(kde.factor * (len(data) / len(a)) ** 0.2)   # Scott's bandwidth of the original n
    dens = kde(grid)
    peaks = [i for i in range(1, len(grid) - 1) if dens[i] > dens[i - 1] and dens[i] >= dens[i + 1]]
    peaks += [i for i, j in [(0, 1), (len(grid) - 1, len(grid) - 2)] if dens[i] > dens[j]]
    return sorted(float(v) for v in np.round(grid[sorted(peaks, key=lambda i: -dens[i])[:2]], 1))
for n in [250, 900]:
    syn = np.sign(rng_kde.random(n) - 0.5) * (90 - np.abs(rng_kde.normal(0, 25, n)))
    syn = np.clip(syn, -90, 90)
    print(f"synthetic, n = {n}: Scott KDE peaks {kde_peaks(syn)}; reflected KDE peaks {kde_peaks(syn, True)}")
rows = []
for sub, g in list(E.groupby("subject")) + [("pooled", E)]:
    pk = kde_peaks(g.angle.values, True)
    rows.append({"subject": sub, "criterion_KDE_peaks": kde_peaks(g.angle.values), "reflected_KDE_peaks": pk,
                 "reflected_within_15_of_pm90": len(pk) == 2 and pk[0] <= -75 and pk[1] >= 75})
kr = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(kr.to_string(index=False))
print("Reflected KDE: two highest maxima within 15 degrees of -90 and +90 in",
      int(kr[kr.subject != "pooled"].reflected_within_15_of_pm90.sum()), "of 12 subjects; pooled",
      bool(kr[kr.subject == "pooled"].reflected_within_15_of_pm90.iloc[0]))

Result: partially reproduced. More than half of the reaches last under 2 s and cover under 200 pixels pooled (0.918 and 0.915) and in all 12 subjects. The angle part does not hold: the two highest maxima of the angle density lie at -71.5 and 75.0 degrees pooled, and within 15 degrees of +-90 in no subject (S02 and S04 have a single maximum, and in S03, S06 and S07 the density at 0 exceeds the lower peak); 22.9% of reaches lie within 30 degrees of horizontal. With a KDE reflected at -90 and +90 (a sensitivity output, not the criterion), the two highest maxima lie within 15 degrees of +-90 pooled and in 6 of 12 subjects, not more than half. On synthetic angles whose density peaks at +-90 the criterion's KDE puts the peaks at -72.5 and 70.0 (n = 250) and at -73.5 and 74.0 degrees (n = 900), so part of the shortfall comes from the KDE's boundary bias.

Claim fig2-bimanual-skew¶

Bimanual ratio and bimanual overlap are skewed toward unimanual movement of the contralateral arm, less so for subjects 02, 04 and 05, while the bimanual class is mostly bimanual.

In [26]:
def bim_table(E):
    rows = []
    for sub, g in list(E.groupby("subject")) + [("pooled", E)]:
        rows.append({"subject": sub, "median_ratio": round(g.bimanual_ratio.median(), 3),
                     "ratio_skewed": g.bimanual_ratio.median() < 0.5,
                     "overlap_skewness": round(stats.skew(g.bimanual_overlap), 3),
                     "overlap_skewed": stats.skew(g.bimanual_overlap) > 0,
                     "share_class_bimanual": round(g.bimanual_class.mean(), 3),
                     "class_mostly_bimanual": g.bimanual_class.mean() > 0.5})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
for label, E_ in [("b", ev[ev.keep_b]), ("a", ev)]:
    bt = bim_table(E_)
    subj = bt[bt.subject != "pooled"]
    pool = bt[bt.subject == "pooled"].iloc[0]
    top_ratio = subj.sort_values("median_ratio", ascending=False).subject.head(5).tolist()
    low_skew = subj.sort_values("overlap_skewness").subject.head(5).tolist()
    named = all(s in top_ratio for s in ["02", "04", "05"]) and all(s in low_skew for s in ["02", "04", "05"])
    print(f"Reading {label}")
    print(bt.to_string(index=False))
    print(f"ratio part: pooled {pool.ratio_skewed}, subjects {int(subj.ratio_skewed.sum())}/12; overlap part: pooled "
          f"{pool.overlap_skewed}, subjects {int(subj.overlap_skewed.sum())}/12; class part: pooled {pool.class_mostly_bimanual}, "
          f"subjects {int(subj.class_mostly_bimanual.sum())}/12")
    print(f"five highest median ratios {top_ratio}; five lowest overlap skewness {low_skew}; S02, S04, S05 in both: {named}\n")

Claim extfig2-1c-contralateral-larger¶

Across all 12 subjects, the median displacement of the contralateral wrist after movement onset is substantially greater than that of the ipsilateral wrist, confirming that event detection mainly picked contralateral movements.

In [27]:
t_pose = np.round(np.arange(91) / ajile.POSE_HZ + ajile.POSE_WIN[0], 3)
post = (t_pose >= 0) & (t_pose <= 1.5)
def disp(tr, reading):
    base = np.nanmean(tr[:, :16], 1) if reading == "a" else tr[:, 45]   # -1.5 to -1 s, or onset
    return np.linalg.norm(tr - base[:, None], axis=2)
rows = []
for sub in SUBJECTS:
    ss = [s for s in sessions if s["subject"] == sub]
    contra = "R_Wrist" if ss[0]["reach_event_desc"] == "r_wrist" else "L_Wrist"
    ipsi = "L_Wrist" if contra == "R_Wrist" else "R_Wrist"
    keep = np.concatenate([ev[(ev.subject == sub) & (ev.day == s["day"])].keep_b.values for s in ss])
    row = {"subject": sub, "contra": contra}
    for reading in ["a", "b"]:
        c = np.concatenate([disp(s["wrist"][contra], reading) for s in ss])[keep]
        i_ = np.concatenate([disp(s["wrist"][ipsi], reading) for s in ss])[keep]
        cm, im = np.nanmedian(c, 0)[post].max(), np.nanmedian(i_, 0)[post].max()
        row[f"{reading}_contra_peak_px"] = round(cm, 1)
        row[f"{reading}_ipsi_peak_px"] = round(im, 1)
        row[f"{reading}_ratio"] = round(cm / im, 2)
    rows.append(row)
cw = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(cw.to_string(index=False))
for r in ["a", "b"]:
    print(f"reading {r}: contralateral peak larger in {(cw[f'{r}_contra_peak_px'] > cw[f'{r}_ipsi_peak_px']).sum()} of 12; "
          f"ratio min {cw[f'{r}_ratio'].min()}, median {cw[f'{r}_ratio'].median()}")

Claim extfig2-2-feature-correlations¶

Over all events, reach magnitude correlates with reach duration (r = 0.26) and onset speed (r = 0.56), reach duration with bimanual overlap (r = 0.48), and the bimanual features with one another (overlap and ratio 0.51, class and ratio 0.50, overlap and class 0.61).

    ax.set_title(ajile.ROI_NAMES[r], fontsize=9)
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel("time (s)"); axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("frequency (Hz)")
fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes, label="dB (masked)")
plt.show()
print("masked values shown, -1.5 to 1.5 s: range", round(float(masked[..., tsel].min()), 2), "to",
      round(float(masked[..., tsel].max()), 2), "dB; values beyond +-1 dB:", int((np.abs(masked[..., tsel]) > 1).sum()))

masked values shown, -1.5 to 1.5 s: range -1.31 to 0.7 dB; values beyond +-1 dB: 53

Result: reproduced. After masking, the mean over 4-30 Hz is negative and over 50-120 Hz positive in precentral (-0.885 and 0.496 dB), postcentral (-0.890, 0.507) and inferior parietal (-0.663, 0.277) over 0 to 0.5 s, and also at the time bin of onset (reading b). Over 0 to 0.5 s, middle frontal, supramarginal and middle temporal show the same pattern (middle temporal only weakly, -0.005 and +0.003 dB); at the onset bin supramarginal's high-frequency value and middle temporal's low-frequency value are 0.000, so for those two it holds only over 0 to 0.5 s.

Claim fig3-sensorimotor-largest¶

Spectral power changes are largest in precentral, postcentral and inferior parietal regions, and the three temporal regions show minimal movement-related changes.

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). The two readings disagree. Reading a counts 7 regions with low-frequency decreases and 7 with high-frequency increases (no difference); reading b gives 35.2 significant low-frequency bins per frequency against 25.9 high-frequency (low-frequency larger). Supramarginal and superior temporal both have significant 4-30 Hz decreases (30 and 24 bins). With ten other bootstrap seeds, reading a gives 7 against 7 regions every time and reading b 35.0 to 35.6 against 25.5 to 25.8 bins per frequency, so the readings disagree under every seed; supramarginal and superior temporal keep their low-frequency decreases and the pattern of fig3-group-lfb-decrease-hfb-increase holds in the three named regions under every seed.

# The bin count ties four subjects at 3 bins. Tie-break by the width in Hz of the run of the
# spectrum below half its minimum, around the minimum, with linear interpolation between bins.
def width_hz(v, f):
    m = int(np.argmin(v)); h = v[m] / 2
    lo = m
    while lo > 0 and v[lo - 1] < h:
        lo -= 1
    hi = m
    while hi < len(v) - 1 and v[hi + 1] < h:
        hi += 1
    left = f[lo] if lo == 0 else f[lo - 1] + (h - v[lo - 1]) / (v[lo] - v[lo - 1]) * (f[lo] - f[lo - 1])
    right = f[hi] if hi == len(v) - 1 else f[hi] + (h - v[hi]) / (v[hi + 1] - v[hi]) * (f[hi + 1] - f[hi])
    return right - left
whz = {s: round(width_hz(low.loc[s].values.astype(float), FREQS[FREQS <= 46].astype(float)), 1) for s in SUBJECTS}
fewest_hz = sorted(whz, key=lambda s: whz[s])[:3]
print("    width in Hz (interpolated):", whz, "\n    three narrowest:", fewest_hz,
      "; S04 and S08 among them:", "04" in fewest_hz and "08" in fewest_hz)
print("Parts holding:", int(p1.all()) + int(all(p2.values())) + int(all(v[-1] for v in p3.values())) +
      int("04" in fewest and "08" in fewest), "of 4")

            v = g[f"roi_band:precentral:{band}_{bm}"].values
            for stat_name, fn in [("mean", np.mean), ("median", np.median)]:
                est = fn(v)
                key = f"{stat_name}_of_band{bm}"
                row[key] = round(est, 3)
                inside.setdefault(key, []).append(lo <= est <= hi)
        v = g[f"roi_band:precentral:{band}_mean"].values
        boot = np.array([np.mean(v[rng_t1.integers(0, len(v), len(v))]) for _ in range(5000)])
        row["bootstrap_ci_mean_of_bandmean"] = f"{np.percentile(boot, 2.5):.2f} to {np.percentile(boot, 97.5):.2f}"
        rows.append(row)
t1 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(t1.to_string(index=False))
print("\nPoint estimates inside the paper's interval, of 24 subject and band pairs:",
      {k: int(sum(v)) for k, v in inside.items()})
lfb_neg = (t1[t1.band == "LFB"]["mean_of_bandmean"] < 0).sum()
hfb_pos = (t1[t1.band == "HFB"]["mean_of_bandmean"] > 0).sum()
print(f"LFB below baseline in {lfb_neg} of 12 subjects; HFB above in {hfb_pos} of 12 (mean of band mean)")

Regression claims (Figure 6 and Extended Data Figure 6-2)¶

The method is the claims file's opening comment: per subject, good electrode and band, forward selection by OLS adjusted R2 over the design columns, then 200 day-balanced splits (90/10, Methods) with a Huber fit of the full model and, for the Delta R2 of each selected feature, a refit with that feature shuffled among the training events. The fits minimise sklearn's HuberRegressor objective (the code's model), many at a time (helper huber_fit); the first cell compares them with sklearn. Delta R2 refits are run where the full model's R2 exceeds 0.05 in either band, the electrodes Figure 6c-d show (legend); elsewhere only R2, coefficients and selection are used. The variants the claims name are run beside the main analysis: the code's 80/20 split, the code's band median, the code's Delta R2 (refit scored on shuffled test events), the code's selection of electrodes by LFB R2, and the code's inclusion of bad electrodes. The code's log(x + 1) transforms are not run as a variant.

In [41]:

# The batched Huber fit (helper huber_fit) against sklearn's HuberRegressor, which the code uses,
# on the first 20 splits of one electrode per subject (the electrode whose LFB power correlates
# best with reach angle), with the columns forward selection keeps.
from sklearn.linear_model import HuberRegressor
rows = []
for sub in SUBJECTS:
    X, groups = design[sub]
    Xn = X.to_numpy(float)
    y = Y[(sub, "mean", "lfb")][:, int(np.nanargmax(np.abs(np.corrcoef(X["angle"], Y[(sub, "mean", "lfb")].T)[0, 1:])))]
    cols = sorted(ajile.forward_select(Xn, y))
    Z = np.column_stack([Xn[:, cols], np.ones(len(y))])
    tr, te = splits[sub][0.9]
    W, _ = ajile.huber_fit(Z[tr[:20]], y[tr[:20]])
    for k in range(20):
        m = HuberRegressor().fit(Z[tr[k], :-1], y[tr[k]])
        rows.append({"subject": sub, "coef_diff": np.abs(np.r_[m.coef_, m.intercept_] - W[k]).max(),
                     "r2_diff": abs(m.score(Z[te[k], :-1], y[te[k]]) - ajile._r2(y[te[k]], Z[te[k]] @ W[k]))})
hc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"{len(hc)} fits: largest coefficient difference {hc.coef_diff.max():.2e}, largest withheld R2 difference "
      f"{hc.r2_diff.max():.2e} (median {hc.r2_diff.median():.1e})")

240 fits: largest coefficient difference 1.16e-03, largest withheld R2 difference 4.40e-05 (median 1.9e-06)
In [43]:
# The models. Stage 1 fits the full model for every electrode and band (forward selection and
# 200 splits); the Delta R2 refits are needed only where the full model's R2 exceeds 0.05 (the
# electrodes Figure 6c-d show), so stage 2 refits those, in both bands. The same for the code's
# 80/20 split (good electrodes), and the full model for the code's median band power.
def seed_of(sub, e, band, variant):
    return int(sub) * 100000 + e * 100 + (band == "hfb") * 10 + variant

def fit(keys, meas, per_train, full_only, variant):
    jobs = []
    for sub, e, band in keys:
        X, groups = design[sub]
        tr, te = splits[sub][per_train]
        jobs.append((X, groups, Y[(sub, meas, band)][:, e], tr, te, seed_of(sub, e, band, variant), full_only))
    rows = []
    for (sub, e, band), out in zip(keys, ajile.run_models(jobs)):
        row = {"subject": sub, "electrode": e, "band": band, "good": bool(first_good[sub][e])}
        if out is None:
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        row.update({"r2": out["r2"], "selected": out["selected"]})
        row.update({f"coef:{f}": v for f, v in out["coef"].items()})
        row.update({f"coefsdm:{f}": v for f, v in out["coef_sd_of_mean"].items()})
        row.update({f"keep:{f}": v for f, v in out["keep_prob"].items()})
        if not full_only:
            row.update({f"dr2:{f}": v for f, v in out["delta_r2"].items()})
            row.update({f"dr2code:{f}": v for f, v in out["delta_r2_code"].items()})
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def two_stage(meas, per_train, electrodes, variant):
    keys = [(sub, e, band) for sub in SUBJECTS for e in electrodes(sub) for band in ["lfb", "hfb"]]
    full = fit(keys, meas, per_train, True, variant)
    over = full[full.r2 > 0.05][["subject", "electrode"]].drop_duplicates()
    keys2 = [(s_, e, band) for s_, e in over.itertuples(index=False) for band in ["lfb", "hfb"]]
    refit = fit(keys2, meas, per_train, False, variant)
    out = full.merge(refit[["subject", "electrode", "band"] + [c for c in refit if c.startswith("dr2")]],
                     on=["subject", "electrode", "band"], how="left")
    assert np.allclose(full.set_index(["subject", "electrode", "band"]).loc[refit.set_index(["subject", "electrode", "band"]).index].r2,
                       refit.r2)
    return out, len(keys), len(keys2)

started = time.time()
reg, n1, n2 = two_stage("mean", 0.9, lambda sub: range(n_el[sub]), 0)
t_main = time.time() - started
reg82, m1, m2 = two_stage("mean", 0.8, lambda sub: np.nonzero(first_good[sub])[0], 1)
t_82 = time.time() - started - t_main
regmed = fit([(sub, e, band) for sub in SUBJECTS for e in np.nonzero(first_good[sub])[0] for band in ["lfb", "hfb"]],
             "median", 0.9, True, 2)

Claim fig6b-best-models-sensorimotor¶

Regression models with the highest withheld R2 are mainly at electrodes over frontoparietal sensorimotor areas, for both bands.

In [45]:
FP5 = ["middle frontal", "precentral", "postcentral", "inferior parietal", "supramarginal"]
SM3 = ["precentral", "postcentral", "inferior parietal"]
TEMP = ["superior temporal", "middle temporal", "inferior temporal"]
raw_w = {sub: ajile.roi_weights(roi_mats[sub], first_good[sub], normalise=False) for sub in SUBJECTS}
def region_of(sub, e):
    w = raw_w[sub][e]
    return ajile.ROI_NAMES[int(np.argmax(w))] if w.sum() > 0 else "none"
for d in (G, reg, reg82):
    d["region"] = [region_of(s_, e) for s_, e in zip(d.subject, d.electrode)]

def project(d, col):
    """Projection-weighted mean over each subject's good electrodes, then the mean over subjects."""
    per = []
    for sub in SUBJECTS:
        v = np.zeros(n_el[sub])
        x = d[d.subject == sub]
        v[x.electrode.values] = np.nan_to_num(x[col].values.astype(float))
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
            per.append(weights[sub].T @ v)
    return pd.Series(np.nanmean(per, 0), index=ajile.ROI_NAMES), pd.Series(np.sum(np.isfinite(per), 0), index=ajile.ROI_NAMES)

holds6b = {}
for band in ["lfb", "hfb"]:
    d = G[G.band == band]
    hi = d[d.r2 > 0.05]
    proj, n_sub = project(d, "r2")
    tab = pd.DataFrame({"electrodes": d.groupby("region").size(), "R2_over_0.05": hi.groupby("region").size(),
                        "median_R2": d.groupby("region").r2.median().round(4), "projected_R2": proj.round(4),
                        "subjects_covering": n_sub}).fillna(0)
    print(f"{band.upper()}:\n{tab.to_string()}")
    share = hi.region.isin(FP5).mean()
    med_sm, med_t = d[d.region.isin(SM3)].r2.median(), d[d.region.isin(TEMP)].r2.median()
    top3 = list(proj.sort_values(ascending=False).index[:3])
    a = bool(share > 0.5 and med_sm > med_t)
    b = all(r in FP5 for r in top3)
    holds6b[band] = (a, b)
    print(f"  reading a: {len(hi)} electrodes with R2 > 0.05, share in the five frontoparietal regions {share:.3f}; "
          f"median R2 sensorimotor {med_sm:.4f} against temporal {med_t:.4f}; holds {a}")
    print(f"  reading b: three highest projected R2 {top3}; all frontoparietal: {b}")
print("Holds (reading a, reading b):", holds6b)

Claim fig6c-angle-and-day-most-informative¶

Reach angle and day of recording are the most informative features for single-event power, especially for low-frequency power.

In [46]:
FEAT_ORDER = ["angle", "day", "duration", "magnitude", "speed", "speech", "bimanual_ratio", "bimanual_overlap",
              "bimanual_class", "time_of_day"]
def ranked(d, band, prefix, select_band=None, fn=np.median):
    """Median over electrodes with R2 > 0.05 (in `select_band`, default the same band) of a per-feature column."""
    sb = select_band or band
    ok = d[(d.band == sb) & (d.r2 > 0.05)][["subject", "electrode"]]
    x = d[d.band == band].merge(ok, on=["subject", "electrode"])
    vals = pd.Series({f: fn(x[f"{prefix}{f}"].values) for f in FEAT_ORDER})
    return vals.sort_values(ascending=False), len(x)
variants6c = [("main", G, "dr2:", None), ("code's Delta R2", G, "dr2code:", None),
              ("code's selection by LFB R2", G, "dr2:", "lfb"), ("code's 80/20 split", reg82[reg82.good], "dr2:", None),
              ("with bad electrodes", reg, "dr2:", None)]
tabs, top2 = {}, {}
for name, d, prefix, sb in variants6c:
    for band in ["lfb", "hfb"]:
        v, n = ranked(d, band, prefix, sb)
        tabs[(name, band.upper(), n)] = v.round(4)
        top2[(name, band)] = list(v.dropna().index[:2])
print("Median Delta R2 over electrodes with R2 > 0.05 (variant, band, electrodes):")
print(pd.DataFrame(tabs).loc[FEAT_ORDER].to_string())
for k, v in top2.items():
    print(f"  {k[0]}, {k[1].upper()}: two largest {v}; angle and day both: {set(v) == {'angle', 'day'}}")

Over good electrodes with R2 > 0.05 in the band, the median reach-angle coefficient is -1.027 in LFB (22 electrodes, 95.5% negative) and 0.535 in HFB (14 electrodes, none negative). The code's selection by LFB R2 gives -1.027 and 0.202, bad electrodes included -0.815 and 0.515, and the 80/20 split -0.973 and 0.540, so the signs hold in every variant. By subject the LFB medians are -1.353 to 0 (4 subjects) and the HFB medians 0 to 0.730 (6 subjects).

Claim fig6d-angle-and-day-largest-coefficients¶

Reach angle and day of recording have the largest coefficient magnitudes among the features, and the SD of the recording-day coefficients is large.

Electrodes selected by the stored R2 (sensitivity, not the criterion). The electrodes with R2 > 0.05 here and those with stored R2 > 0.05 overlap in 18 electrodes in LFB (22 here, 23 stored) and 12 in HFB (14 here, 22 stored). The stored sets come from 5 subjects in LFB and 8 in HFB, against 4 and 6 here. With the stored selection, 22 of 23 LFB and 18 of 22 HFB electrodes are in the five frontoparietal regions (fig6b, reading a, share part). Angle (0.063) and day (0.013) have the two largest median Delta R2 in LFB, and day (0.050) and angle (0.019) in HFB, with the code's Delta R2 too (fig6c). The median angle coefficient is -1.026 in LFB and +0.498 in HFB (fig6d, upward reaches). Angle and the day SD are the two largest coefficient values under both readings in both bands (fig6d, largest coefficients). The fig6b-d results are the same on either set of electrodes. Taken as the SD of the split-averaged one-hot coefficients, not the mean over splits of the per-split SD, the day value is 0.658 against 0.660 in LFB and 0.729 against 0.733 in HFB, and angle and day stay the two largest.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The paper's preprocessing, event pruning and visual removal of false positives were done before the data were deposited; the dataset holds 8088 events and marks none as false positives, so all are kept, for the behavioural claims and for every ECoG claim. The bad-segment rules use an assumed summary of segment power; with only segments with missing samples dropped, the across-subject tests, the day effects and the Table 1 outcome (22 of 24 inside) do not change (last data check above). Region power uses the paper's Figshare projection matrices, not a new projection from the AAL atlas. Bad electrodes are those of each subject's first file. The Morlet transform is computed by FFT and matches MNE's direct convolution. The regression models minimise the objective of sklearn's HuberRegressor by a batched Newton method, which matches sklearn's fits to 4.4e-05 in withheld R2; Delta R2 refits are run only at electrodes whose full-model R2 exceeds 0.05, the electrodes Figure 6c-d show. The day and time-of-day coefficient is the mean over splits of the SD of their one-hot coefficients; the SD of the split-averaged coefficients changes it by at most 0.004. On the electrodes selected by the R2 stored in the files, the fig6b-d results are the same. The code's log(x + 1) transforms of reach magnitude and onset speed are not run as a variant. In the code's Delta R2 variant the refit is shared with the main version and only the test events are shuffled.

What was found about the dataset. (1) In three files (S01 day 7, S04 day 3, S06 day 3) the ECoG covers only the end of the day but its starting_time is 0, while the event table and pose use a clock from midnight; the ECoG must be shifted by 8.1 to 8.5 h, as ReachEvents and the neural response show. (2) The files hold 8088 events; the data descriptor states 6931 verified events, and the paper's counts per subject are lower than the files'. (3) The reach angle is stored in image coordinates (upward negative) and unfolded, without saying so. (4) The pose is labelled meters but is in pixels. (5) session_start_time gives midnight UTC labelled as 19:00 at UTC-5. (6) Bimanual overlap is described as a fraction but reaches 3.83 (it is in seconds). (7) 124 event segments contain missing ECoG samples. (8) Sex and age are not recorded. (9) Seven subjects have electrode groups described as depth, where the paper says five.
